head: cloud/json-enum-mixed-checks
title: fix(json): keep mixed string and number enum values reachable
body:
When `JsonConstraint` compiles a finite `enum`/`const`, it validates each candidate value against its schema with a cached `JsonSchemaLexeme`. The cache (`value_checks_`) was keyed by schema pointer alone. A schema without a single `type`, such as an `anyOf` of string and integer, can receive both a string and a number. The first value seen fixed the cached check to a String or Number lexeme, and every later value of the other kind was rejected as if it did not match.

Example: with `{"x":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"integer"}]}}` and `"enum":[{"x":"a"},{"x":1}]`, the grammar admitted `{"x":"a"}` but not `{"x":1}`. Reversing the enum order flipped which value was lost. The model was forced onto a subset of a valid enum. It could not emit invalid JSON.

Change: the cache key is `(schema, value is a string)`, so strings and numbers each get their own check.

Test: `json_constraint_test` adds `TestMixedEnumValues`. It checks both enum orders on an object property, plus an array enum `[["a",1]]` whose items are an `anyOf` of string and number. On unpatched main it fails at the first ordering (`{"x":1}` is rejected).

Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.
